new_entities.name: Probiotic supplementation in infancy
new_entities.description: Probiotic supplementation given during infancy, often alongside maternal prenatal or lactation supplementation.

new_entities.name: Atopic dermatitis by 2 years of age
new_entities.description: Atopic dermatitis or eczema occurring during infancy and the first two years of life.

edges.effect_quant: The most reproducible benefit of early-life probiotics is a modest reduction in eczema within the first 2 years, with much less confidence that protection persists later or generalizes across every strain strategy.
edges.population: infants receiving probiotics directly and/or through paired maternal-plus-infant supplementation
edges.mechanism: Early probiotic exposure may shift gut microbial colonization and immune education toward a less pro-atopic phenotype during the first months of life. The strain-specific and time-limited nature of the signal suggests this is a narrow early-window effect rather than a universal allergy reset.
edges.summary: The pooled literature supports a small early-eczema benefit, but not a sweeping allergy-prevention claim. Meta-analyses repeatedly show lower atopic dermatitis incidence up to about age 2, especially when mixed lactobacillus-bifidobacterium strategies and maternal-plus-infant exposure are used, yet the durability and strain generalizability remain uneven.
edges.caveats: This edge is sensitive to strain, timing, and whether mothers were supplemented during pregnancy as well. It should not be read as proof that any probiotic product prevents eczema, only that the broader intervention class has shown a modest early signal in pooled trials.
